title: Documents and spreadsheets
covers: README files, guides, reports, proposals, invoices, slide decks, Word, PDF and spreadsheet files someone opens and reads or edits.

stakeholders.who: The person who opens the file: a client, the owner, or a beginner following setup steps
cares_about: finding the one thing they need
steps that work on their own machine
would_notice: a repair prompt, a broken image or raw markdown symbols
a command that fails on the first try
a wall of text without headings

stakeholders.who: The person who checks the numbers or facts (for example a bookkeeper or a reviewer)
cares_about: units and dates that cannot be misread
would_notice: a total that does not equal its rows
a column without unit or currency
a figure that differs between two pages
a real password or key in the file

stakeholders.who: The person who updates the document or spreadsheet next
cares_about: knowing what changed and what is still open
would_notice: typed-in numbers where a formula should be

first_ten_seconds: Open the file in the app the reader will use: does it open cleanly and look finished?
Can you find the summary or the first step without scrolling?
Pick one number or one command and check it: is it right?

checks.claim: The file opens in the app the reader will use (Word, Excel, a PDF reader, the GitHub or docs renderer) with no repair prompt, missing fonts, broken images or raw markup.
checks.how_to_inspect: Open the final file in the target app (render a Markdown file in its real viewer) and page through all of it.
checks.evidence_required: A screenshot of the opened file and the app or viewer used.

source.rationale: A file that does not open cleanly is unusable whatever its content, and it is the first thing the reader meets.

checks.claim: Every command, path and flag in the document was run or checked against the real code, not written from memory of the plan.
checks.how_to_inspect: Run every command in the document, or open the code that defines it, and tick each one.
checks.evidence_required: The list of commands with their exit codes or the file and line that defines each.

source.quote: Every documented command/path was actually verified against the real code

checks.claim: Steps give the exact command, path and expected result, in order, with nothing the reader has to guess.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read each step and ask what a beginner would type; any step that needs a guess is rewritten.

source.quote: Setup instructions give exact commands and exact file paths

checks.claim: Setup or how-to steps were followed from a clean start (new folder, another user or a VM), not only on the author's machine.
checks.how_to_inspect: Follow the document literally in a clean folder or sandbox and note every step that needed knowledge not in the text.
checks.evidence_required: The transcript of the clean run and the steps that had to be fixed (N/A for documents without steps).

source.section: 3. "Would this person look at this?" examples

checks.claim: The structure lets a reader find one thing fast: a short summary first, clear headings, one topic per section.
checks.how_to_inspect: Read only the headings and the first lines; check you can find each main task from them alone.

source.quote: Structure lets a reader scan for the one command/section they need.

checks.claim: No shorthand, codenames or jargon the reader was never told about.
checks.how_to_inspect: Mark every term a newcomer would have to look up and explain or replace it.

source.quote: no invented shorthand or unexplained jargon

checks.claim: Totals equal the sum of their parts, percentages add up, and the same figure has the same value everywhere in the document.
checks.how_to_inspect: Re-add every total and compare each repeated figure across pages, tables and charts.
checks.evidence_required: The recalculation per total (or the formula check) and any mismatches fixed.

source.rationale: A checker's first move is to re-add one column; a single mismatch voids trust in every other number.

checks.claim: Every number shows its unit or currency, decimals are consistent per column, and dates cannot be misread (24 Oct 2026 or 2026-10-24, never 10/11/12).
checks.how_to_inspect: Scan every table, column header and chart axis for a unit and every date for an unambiguous format.
checks.evidence_required: The columns, axes and dates fixed.

checks.claim: No real secret, token, password or personal data that should not travel with the file; only placeholders.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the file, including hidden sheets, comments, speaker notes and metadata, for key, token, password, e-mail addresses and account numbers.
checks.evidence_required: The search command and its output (zero hits, or each hit fixed).

source.quote: No real secret value, token, or credential appears anywhere in the doc

checks.claim: Computed cells are formulas, inputs are kept apart from calculations, and no cell shows an error such as #REF!, #DIV/0! or #N/A.
checks.how_to_inspect: Show formulas and scan each computed column; search all sheets for cells starting with '#' (N/A for documents without a spreadsheet).
checks.evidence_required: A screenshot of the formula view and the error search.

source.rationale: A pasted value looks right today and goes silently wrong the first time an input changes.

checks.claim: Spreadsheets have a frozen header row, readable column widths, number formats, and sheet names that say what they hold.
checks.how_to_inspect: Open each sheet, scroll down and right, and look at headers, widths, formats and tab names.
checks.evidence_required: A screenshot of each sheet scrolled (N/A for documents without a spreadsheet).

source.rationale: These are the settings a professional makes in the first minute; their absence is how a sheet reads as unfinished.

checks.claim: The document states its date or version, the source of each outside figure, and what was verified versus assumed.
checks.how_to_inspect: Find the date or version line, a source for every external figure, and a verified-versus-assumed note.
checks.evidence_required: Where each of those three appears.

source.quote: What was verified vs. assumed is stated explicitly.

checks.claim: Printed or PDF output has page numbers, no table rows split across pages, and nothing cut off at the margins.
checks.how_to_inspect: Print to PDF and page through it at full size.
checks.evidence_required: The PDF path and any page fixed (N/A when the file is never printed).

source.rationale: Contracts, invoices and reports still get printed, and a cut-off column is visible on paper at once.

checks.claim: Any action still needed from the owner (a missing key, an open decision) is called out near the top, not buried.
checks.how_to_inspect: Search the document for open items and check each appears in one clearly headed place.
checks.evidence_required: The location of the open-items list.

source.quote: Any owner action still required (missing key, unresolved TODO) is called out, not buried.

checks.claim: The document describes what actually shipped, including where it differs from the plan.
checks.how_to_inspect: Compare the document with the final diff or delivered files and list any difference.
checks.evidence_required: The differences found and how the text now covers them.

source.quote: Deviations from the original plan are reflected, not silently ignored.

common_sloppy_defects.symptom: steps that only work with the author's paths, cache or logged-in accounts

common_sloppy_defects.defect: Totals that do not add up
common_sloppy_defects.symptom: the total row differs from the sum of the rows above it
a total typed in by hand, so it no longer changes when an input changes
a column of numbers with no currency, unit or period
03/04/2026, which is March to one reader and April to another
Sheet1, no frozen header, ##### in narrow columns, raw ** and # in a rendered document
